user:
Task: Write a compact study note comparing the three cache-write policies below, including a Markdown table with columns Policy | When memory is written | Trade-off.

Provided notes:
- Write-through: every write goes to the cache and to main memory at the same time. Simple and always consistent, but every write pays the slow memory latency.
- Write-back: writes go only to the cache and are marked dirty; memory is updated when the line is evicted. Fast writes, but memory can be stale and eviction is more complex.
- Write-around: writes skip the cache and go straight to memory; only reads populate the cache. Avoids caching write-once data, but a subsequent read of just-written data misses.
